title: The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids
title_html:
The Wolf and the
Seven Young Kids
source: Grimm, Household Tales, tr. Margaret Hunt (1884), tale 5
lesson: Trust is good. Checking is better.
lines: Mother Goat had to go out. Seven kids, she said, don't open the door to the wolf. He has a rough voice and black feet.
Knock, knock. Open up, it's Mummy! You're not Mummy, said the kids. Your voice is rough!
So the wolf ate chalk to make his voice soft. But the kids saw a black paw at the window. Not Mummy!
So he had a baker smear dough on his feet, and a miller dust them with flour. White paws! The kids opened up.
They hid everywhere: under the table, in the bed, in the oven. The wolf gobbled up six, and fell asleep under a tree. Only the youngest, hiding in the clock, was safe.
Mother came home, found the wolf snoring, snipped him open, and out hopped all six kids! They filled his belly with stones.
The wolf woke up thirsty, leaned over the well, and splash! Trust is good. Checking is better.
Next time: Faithful John, the most loyal servant ever. Follow so you don't miss it!
